title: Asymmetric rolling upgrade rehearsal and deprecation matrix
body:
Summary:

This doc is a working rehearsal plan and compatibility/deprecation matrix for performing asymmetric rolling upgrades across Private deployments (VPC and on-prem appliances). The focus is on minimizing disruption for mixed-cluster topologies where control plane components and runtime nodes may be on staggered schedules, and where clients (APIs) can be pinned to older API contracts.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable rehearsal sequence for upgrades that crosses control plane, runtime, and terraform module changes.
- Define compatibility levels (runtime, api, terraform) and a deprecation timeline per feature/flag.
- Capture clear rollback steps that are executable during partial-failure scenarios.
- Surface test harnesses and smoke checks that map to SLOs and business-critical flows.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to Private deployments (VPC-connected clusters and on-prem appliance bundles).
- We assume customers may have heterogenous node types (k8s with GPU nodes, bare-metal inference appliances).
- We assume some customers will run old API clients for up to 90 days after control plane upgrade.
- Terraform modules will be bumped but kept backward-compatible for a deprecation window; we must document the shim path.

High-level upgrade model (asymmetric rolling):
1) Control plane minor upgrade (canary subset of control plane instances)
2) API compatibility layer verification (shims activated)
3) Runtime node rollout in waves by region/hardware class
4) Terraform module apply for infra changes (post-runtime wave; read-only flag set until final wave)
5) Final cutover: feature gates turned on and deprecation flags removed

Compatibility & deprecation matrix (quick view):
- RUNTIME_MAJOR (vX -> vX+1): backward-incompatible kernel changes. Strategy: default to dual-runtime mode with old KV cache format support. Deprecation window: 180 days.
- CONTROL_PLANE_API (vA -> vA+1): additive endpoints OK; breaking changes go through shim with header X-RW-Compat: legacy. Deprecation window: 90 days.
- TERRAFORM_MODULE (vM -> vM+1): state migration required? If yes, require manual preflight export/import. Deprecation window: 120 days.
- MODEL_KV_FORMAT (on-disk): upgraded via background reindex; nodes can serve mixed formats during migration.

Matrix: For each feature being changed, annotate: change_type | compatible_with_old_runtime | requires-shim | terrraform-bump | rollback-safe?
Example entries (short):
- session-cookie-hash | control-plane-only | yes | no | yes
- async-batched-kernel | runtime-kernel | no | yes | partial (see rollback steps)
- tf-module-networking | infra | N/A | yes | no (state migration risky)

Preflight checklist (must pass BEFORE any live canary):
- [ ] terraform plan reviewed and stored: tf-plan-<id> (store in artifacts/upgrade/<date>)
- [ ] smoke harness green on staging with synthetic workloads matching 95th pct load
- [ ] KV cache migration dry-run completed on snapshot (estimate time + tail-latency impact)
- [ ] backward-compatibility tests (api/shim) executed with recorded traffic replay
- [ ] Runbook dry-run: engineers assigned and pager rotations notified
- [ ] Validate DB schema migrations are idempotent and pausable

Rehearsal run sequence (play-by-play):
- Phase 0: Canary rehearsal in isolated lab cluster (non-prod)
  - deploy control plane patch to single replica, enable verbose tracing, collect metrics for 2h
  - run replay for 24h at 25% expected production workload
  - smoke: generation latency, streaming correctness, function-calling sanity

- Phase 1: Production canary (region-low-traffic)
  - choose two customer-sim clusters with non-critical SLAs
  - apply control-plane upgrade to canary nodes only
  - toggle API shim header acceptance (X-RW-Compat: legacy)
  - monitor for 30m at p95/p99 and error rate, then proceed if green

- Phase 2: Runtime waves (by hardware class)
  - wave A: non-GPU/low-memory nodes (20%)
  - wave B: GPU-A nodes (35%)
  - wave C: GPU-B / high-memory (45%)
  - between waves: run data-plane KV reconciliation job and validate index health

- Phase 3: Terraform module gradual apply
  - apply non-disruptive changes (labels, tags, scaling policy) first
  - delay stateful networking or storage schema apply until all runtimes are upgraded or plan approved for blue-green infra swap

Smoke and acceptance tests (short list):
- Tokenized throughput test (p50/p95/p99 latency)
- End-to-end generation with streaming (compare chunk boundaries, token continuity)
- Functional regression suite for safety/filters (sampled by hash)
- Auth/ACL roundtrip checks (KMS/HSM interactions)
- Billing & metering sanity (token counts, rate-limits)

Rollback strategy (asymmetric-aware):
- General principle: roll back the smallest possible surface first (control-plane replica -> runtime nodes -> terraforms). Avoid terraforming 'undo' unless absolutely required.

Control plane partial rollback:
- Step 1: remove recently-deployed control-plane replica from LB (or set cordon flag)
- Step 2: scale down new replica; re-promote an older replica if leader election required
- Step 3: keep API shim active to allow older clients to continue
- Verification: sanity tests same as smoke list, check tracing for dropped requests

Runtime rollback (kernel incompatibility):
- If kernel-level faults present on new runtime wave: autoscale older runtime image in parallel and migrate KV caches via short lived sidecar (read-write fallback).
- If migration cannot be completed within X minutes (TBD), cordon nodes and revert to previous runtime image via image rollback pipeline.

Terraform rollback (stateful):
- If tf apply mutated state in a way that is not trivially reversible (networking, storage), isolate by adding a read-only guard and open an emergency migration task.
- Maintain exported state snapshots before apply and have documented step-by-step restore (terraform state push + force unlock).

Observability & SLO gating:
- Gate progression using automated checks at each step (CI job that runs green -> allow next step)
- Primary signals: request_error_rate, p99_latency, model_inference_errors, kv_reconciliation_backlog, infra_cpu_spike
- Define thresholds: if any signal breaches hard threshold for >5m -> abort and initiate rollback. Soft breaches (transient) require owner signoff.

Runbook snippets / commands (examples):
- Remove node from LB: curl -X POST ${CONTROL_PLANE}/admin/nodes/${NODE_ID}/drain
- Revert runtime image: kubectl set image daemonset/inference inference-node=redwood/runtime:prev-tag -n redwood
- Terraform export: terraform state pull > state-snap-<date>.tfstate

Escalation / communication plan:
- Page on-call SRE first (pager: eng-sre-oncall)
- Email notify: infra-upgrades@redwood.ai with subject [UPGRADE-REHEARSAL] <region> <wave>
- Slack channel: #private-upgrades (use pinned message template)
- Postmortem: 72-hour draft, final within 14 days

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Q1: exact timing for terraform stateful changes — is 2nd runtime wave safe? (Priya to confirm with infra storage owner)
- Q2: how to automate shim header insertion for legacy clients? Should be a header rewrite at edge or a middleware in control plane? (Luis to prototype)
- Q3: clear metric for KV migration progress (need single numeric indicator)

Rehearsal schedule (example):
- Week -2: lab rehearsal, smoke harness tuning
- Week -1: staging end-to-end replay + perf baseline capture
- Day 0: production canary (control plane only), 4h observation window
- Day 1-2: runtime waves with 2h observation between waves
- Day 3: terraform non-stateful apply + final verification

Postmortem template (quick):
- Summary of events
- Timeline with timestamps
- Root cause (technical & process)
- Impacted customers / footprints
- What went well / improvements
- Action items and owners (with ETA)

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- tf-plan artifacts location: s3://redwood-upgrades/plans/<id>
- replay harness: git@github.com:redwood-inference/traffic-replay.git
- test matrix CSV: artifacts/tests/compat-matrix-<date>.csv

This is a working draft. Use this doc to rehearse at least once every quarter for major runtime/terraform milestones. Keep the matrix updated with specific feature flags and deprecation dates as PRs land.

Notes: several of the rollback patterns were inspired by past incidents (see JIRA-ENG-3224). Keep conservatism when terraforming stateful resources — prefer runtime-first approaches where possible.
